title: Rav Huna bar Gurion
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Bereshit Rabbah 26:6 preserves the saying Hyman calls precious: even a staff, even a strap (are under providence). Hyman suggests that the reading should be Rav Chama bar Gurion, as in Kohelet Rabbah 8:9.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Midrash Rabbah — TE digital Bereshit Rabbah 26:6 fully writes Rabbi Huna bar Gurion, while Hyman’s heading fully writes Rav. Its Kohelet Rabbah 8:9 has Rabbi Yonatan making the staff-and-strap statement and Rabbi Chama bar Gurion making the following statement about barren trees. Hyman’s proposed Chama replacement is preserved as his conjecture rather than as an exact identical attribution in that digital parallel.

The checked Bereshit Rabbah 26:6 fully names Rabbi Huna bar Gurion for the staff-and-strap saying. Kohelet Rabbah 8:9 attributes that saying to Rabbi Yonatan and the following saying about barren trees to Rabbi Chama bar Gurion. Hyman’s fully written Rav heading and his proposed Chama reading remain his wording and conjecture, without title or attribution harmonization.
